Definition: to spill forth (blood, a libation, liquid metal; or even a solid, i.e. to mound up); also (figuratively) to expend (life, soul, complaint, money, etc.); intensively, to sprawl out
BiblicalUsage: To pour out can mean to shed blood, to empty a soul, or to give a Spirit. Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed, and Reuben said to his brothers, shed no blood, but cast Joseph into the pit. Hannah poured out her soul before the LORD, Joel promises that God will pour out His Spirit upon all flesh, and the psalm tells the people to pour out their heart before Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe what we pour out shows what fills us, whether it is blood, or a soul, or a heart. Hannah poured out her sorrow and God gave her a son, and Joel's promise is that God will pour out His own Spirit in return. That is why I pour out my heart before Him, because He is a refuge for us.
